headline: Stan Lee and Jack Kirby created the Hulk in 1962
post:
Since 1962, the Hulk has stood as an essential part of the Marvel Universe, evolving from a savage brute into one of the publisher's most iconic figures. According to Screen Rant, Stan Lee and Jack Kirby originally patterned the character after literary figures like Doctor Jekyll and Mister Hyde before a gamma explosion changed scientist Bruce Banner forever. Over the decades, legendary creators shaped Bruce Banner's legacy through unforgettable comic book runs, introducing incredible milestones like the debut of Wolverine alongside writer Len Wein and artist Herb Trimpe. Other visionary creators later explored the monster's complex psyche, featuring major eras like Peter David's record-breaking twelve-year run and Greg Pak's influential "Planet Hulk" storyline. Which classic creative team shaped your favorite era of Marvel's green Goliath?

#Hulk #BruceBanner #MarvelComics
original_title: 9 Hulk Runs That Redefined Bruce Banner

headline: Cyber Scares Wolverine More Than Magneto
post:
Magneto's metal powers make him a terrifying threat to Wolverine, but another villain actually strikes deeper fear into the X-Men hero. Silas Burr, known as Cyber, carries a much darker personal history with Logan from their time together in the Devil's Brigade.

Cyber murdered the woman Logan loved and gouged out his left eye before later receiving his own adamantium skin upgrade. This brutal tormentor holds a powerful psychological grip built on trauma rather than just raw physical strength.

Would you want to face Cyber or Magneto in a fight?

#Wolverine #XMen #Marvel
original_title: There's Only One X-Men Villain Who Scares Wolverine More Than Magneto

headline: Skydance taps ex-Marvel producer Jeremy Latcham
post:
Big changes are coming for DC Studios after a major studio merger under Skydance. James Gunn and Peter Safran are reportedly stepping down as co-heads, leaving the cinematic future uncertain. According to /Film, Skydance CEO David Ellison has installed former Marvel producer Jeremy Latcham as the new president and chief creative officer to help reinvent the franchise. Latcham is known for favoring broad, family-friendly entertainment and previously worked on hits like "Guardians of the Galaxy". Meanwhile, James Gunn is sticking around to finish his Superman sequel "Man of Tomorrow", which is currently set for release on July 9, 2027. With new leadership taking a hard look at recent projects, fans can expect significant updates on upcoming titles very soon. What are you hoping to see from the DC Universe next year?

#DCStudios #JamesGunn #JeremyLatcham
original_title: ​​Big Changes Are Coming To The DC Universe In 2027
